transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I've been dealing with some things at work, and I just wanted to make sure I'm handling everything the right way. I'm a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and... well, I hope this doesn't sound too strange. I really don't want to come across as unreasonable or anything. But for a while now, I've been kind of convinced that certain people in the local arts and finance circles are... quietly tracking which clients I meet with. 

And it feels like they're sending me these little signals about it. You know, just subtle things, like through the event invitations I get, or the panel topics they choose, or even who ends up sitting near me at networking events. 

I keep trying to tell myself it could all just be a coincidence—I mean, I know how it sounds, and I really try to look at it logically—but I just can't really let it go. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing to manage this.
Have you been feeling unusually low, or perhaps significantly more energetic or irritable than is typical for you, during the time you've been having these experiences?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope it's okay to say that, but my mood has actually been pretty steady. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? So I haven't been feeling down or depressed or anything like that. And I'm definitely not, like, overly energetic or snapping at anyone. Even with everything going on, I always try to stay pretty even-keeled and professional with my clients and colleagues. 

Is that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep your thoughts organized or have people mentioned that you seem to be speaking in a way that is hard for them to follow?

Oh, um, no, definitely not. I really hope I haven't been hard to follow today! 

I actually take a lot of pride in being clear, especially with my clients. You know, when you're explaining financial portfolios and retirement plans, you really have to keep your thoughts organized and precise. So... no, nobody has mentioned anything like that to me. I always try to make sure I'm communicating as professionally as possible. 

Am I... making sense to you so far? I just want to be sure I'm being helpful and giving you clear answers, and not rambling or anything.
Aside from the experiences you mentioned, have you ever heard, seen, or smelled things that others around you did not seem to notice?

Um... no, no, I haven't experienced anything like that. I really hope it's okay to say that, but I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. 

I know sometimes people with... well, with stress or other things might have those kinds of experiences, but I've always been very grounded in that way. I mean, my senses are all completely normal. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, totally out of touch with reality or anything. It's really just the... the patterns with the networking things that I mentioned before. 

Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know, and I really hope I'm being a good patient for you today.
Has this situation with the networking events caused you to miss work, lose clients, or change how you interact with your friends or family?

Um, well, I want to be completely honest with you, but I really hope it doesn't make me sound unprofessional. I am absolutely still working. I take my career very seriously, I promise. 

It's just... I guess my practice has gotten a little bit smaller recently. Nothing drastic! It's just that I've been, um, avoiding some of the public panels I usually speak at. And... well, I might have missed a few routine follow-up calls. It's just been a little harder to keep up the exact same level of constant client contact that I used to manage so easily. 

But I'm still doing my best to take care of my core clients, really. I hope that's understandable? I just don't want you to think I'm completely dropping the ball or failing at my job. Am I still doing okay with these answers? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
How long have you been feeling that these people in the arts and finance circles are tracking your client meetings and sending you these signals?

Um, well... I'd say it's been about two months since I really started noticing the signals. 

I know that probably sounds like a long time to let something like this go on, but I really didn't want to jump to conclusions or make a big deal out of nothing. I tried to just ignore it at first, you know, keep my head down and focus on my clients. I didn't want to seem paranoid or unprofessional. It's just that over the last couple of months, the patterns with them tracking my meetings became a bit too obvious to ignore completely. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything. I've been doing my absolute best to manage it quietly. Is... is two months a normal amount of time for something like this? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of timeline.

Aside from these experiences with your professional circles, have you ever felt that anyone else, such as the government, neighbors, or strangers in public, is monitoring you or trying to send you secret messages?

Oh, um, no. No, definitely not. I completely understand why you have to ask that, and I really want to be as helpful as possible today, but... no, nothing like that at all. 

It's really strictly just those specific networking circles I mentioned. The arts and finance people. My neighbors are perfectly fine, and I've never felt like the government or random strangers were paying any attention to me. I always try to be very rational about my surroundings, you know? I wouldn't let my imagination run away with me with things like that. 

I hope it's okay that the answer is no? I just... I really want to assure you that outside of those specific professional issues, everything else in my life is completely normal. I'm just a regular guy going about my day. Does that help give you the right picture? I want to make sure I'm answering everything the way you need me to.
What do you believe is the ultimate goal or intention of these people when they send you these signals?

Um, honestly... I really don't know. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I know you're trying to get a complete picture, and I really want to give you whatever information you need to do your job, but... I haven't actually figured out what they want from me. 

I try very hard not to sit around coming up with, you know, wild theories about it. I definitely don't want to sound like someone who thinks there's some massive, movie-level conspiracy going on. That's really not me. I just notice the signals when they happen, and... well, maybe they just want to throw me off my game a little bit? Or make me second-guess my professional advice? But as for some big, ultimate goal... I really couldn't say. 

Is it alright that I don't have a specific answer for that? I just want to make sure I'm not being unhelpful by not knowing. I'm really trying to be as cooperative as possible.
Have you noticed any changes in your personal hygiene or your ability to keep your home or office environment as tidy as you usually do?

Oh, um, no, not at all. I mean, I try to keep everything very put together. 

I know sometimes when people are dealing with... well, with stress or distractions like I've been having, they might let things slide, but I really pride myself on staying organized. My apartment is clean, I shower every day, my suits are pressed... I always want to make sure I'm presenting myself well, especially for my clients. You know, you can't really be a good financial advisor if you look like you don't have your own life in order, right?

So, yeah, everything on that front is completely normal. I hope that's a good sign? I really try my best to keep up with all my responsibilities, no matter what else is going on. I haven't let any of this affect how I take care of myself or my space. Does that sound okay to you?
Have you ever had any major medical illnesses, or have you used any medications or substances that might have affected your health?

Oh, no, nothing like that. I've been very lucky with my health, actually. 

I don't have any major medical conditions, and I don't take any prescription medications or anything. I mean, maybe an ibuprofen if I get a headache from staring at spreadsheets too long, but that's really it. And as for substances... no, definitely not. I might have a glass of wine at a networking dinner, but I never overdo it. I always need to keep a clear head for my clients, you know? 

I really try to take good care of myself. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to reassure you that there's nothing physical or, um, substance-related that would be causing any issues. Everything is completely clean on that front. Is that helpful?
